He is a {{convert|2.01|m|ftin|abbr=on}} tall [[small forward]]. As a teenager, Kalaitzakis used to be regarded as one of the top young European prospects in his age range. ==Professional career== === Panathinaikos (2016–2021) === After playing with the junior youth clubs of [[Aris B.C.|Aris]], Kalaitzakis began his professional career in 2016, with the Greek club [[Panathinaikos B.C.|Panathinaikos]]. With Panathinaikos, he won the [[Greek Basketball Cup|Greek Cup]] title in 2016, 2017, and 2019, and also the [[Greek Basket League|Greek League]] championship, in 2017, 2018 and 2019. In March 2018, Kalaitzakis announced his intention to declare for the [[2018 NBA draft]].{{Cite web |last=Givony |first=Jonathan |date=March 26, 2018 |title=Greek guard Kalaitzakis to declare for NBA |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/22913797/georgios-kalaitzakis-greece-declare-nba-draft |access-date=July 2, 2024 |website=ESPN.com}} He later withdrew from the draft before the draft's withdrawal deadline. ==== Nevėžis (2019–2020) ==== On August 28, 2019, Kalaitzakis signed with [[BC Nevėžis|Nevėžis Kėdainiai]] of the [[Lithuanian Basketball League]], on a [[loan (sports)|loan]] deal from Panathinaikos.{{Cite web|url=https://www.kknevezis.lt/prie-komandos-jungiasi-talentingieji-broliai-kalaitzakia/|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190828072836/https://www.kknevezis.lt/prie-komandos-jungiasi-talentingieji-broliai-kalaitzakia/|url-status=dead|archive-date=2019-08-28|title=Prie komandos jungiasi talentingieji broliai Kalaitzakiai|date=August 28, 2019|publisher=BC Nevėžis Official Website|language=Lithuanian|access-date=August 28, 2019}} In 23 games played in the Lithuanian league's [[2019–20 LKL season|2019–20 season]], he averaged 12.2 points, 4.3 rebounds, 2.3 assists and 1 steal in 28.7 minutes per game.{{Cite web|url=https://en.lkl.lt/zaidejai/georgios-kalaitzakis|title=Georgios Kalaitzakis - LKL.LT|website=en.lkl.lt}} In April 2020, Kalaitzakis declared for the [[2020 NBA draft]].{{Cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/29024141/greek-guard-georgios-kalaitzakis-declares-nba-draft|title=Greek guard Kalaitzakis declares for NBA draft|date=April 11, 2020|website=ESPN.com}} However, he withdrew before the draft took place. ==== Return to Panathinaikos (2020–2021) ==== On August 11, 2020, Kalaitzakis re-signed with [[Panathinaikos B.C.|Panathinaikos]] through the end of the 2021–2022 season.{{Cite web|url=https://www.euroleaguebasketball.net/euroleague/news/|title=Latest News | Euroleague|website=Euroleague Basketball|date=19 October 2023 }}{{cite news |title=Panathinaikos re-signs Giorgos Kalaitzakis until 2022 |url=https://sportando.basketball/en/panathinaikos-re-signs-giorgos-kalaitzakis-until-2022/ |newspaper=Sportando |accessdate=August 11, 2020 |date=August 11, 2020}} With Panathinaikos, he went on to win both the [[2020–21 Greek Basketball Cup|2020–21 Greek Cup]] title and the [[2020–21 Greek Basket League]] championship. ===Milwaukee Bucks (2021)=== Kalaitzakis was selected by the [[NBA]]'s [[Indiana Pacers]], with the 60th overall pick of the [[2021 NBA draft]]. His draft rights were then traded to the [[Milwaukee Bucks]], along with the draft rights of the 54th pick, [[Sandro Mamukelashvili]], and two second-round draft picks, for [[Isaiah Todd]].{{Cite web|url=https://www.wqow.com/sports/bucks-acquire-draft-rights-to-2-players-in-trade-with-pacers/article_138b9a9b-9db2-5ad7-b5e5-25a76143e6a5.html|title=Bucks acquire draft rights to 2 players in trade with Pacers|first=Nick|last=Tabbert|website=WQOW|date=30 July 2021 }} Kalaitzakis' contract with [[Panathinaikos B.C.|Panathinaikos]] had a buyout amount of $300,000, which was paid by the Bucks.{{Cite web|url=https://www.sport24.gr/basket/apochorei-apo-ton-panathinaiko-o-kalaitzakis-gia-na-diekdikisei-thesi-sto-roster-ton-milgoyoki-mpaks.9310976.html|title=Αποχωρεί από τον Παναθηναϊκό ο Καλαϊτζάκης για να διεκδικήσει θέση στο ρόστερ των Μιλγουόκι Μπακς|website=www.sport24.gr}} On August 11, 2021, the Milwaukee Bucks announced that they had signed Kalaitzakis.{{cite web|title=Milwaukee Bucks Sign Georgios Kalaitzakis|url=https://www.nba.com/bucks/news/milwaukee-bucks-sign-georgios-kalaitzakis|date=August 11, 2021|website=NBA.com|accessdate=August 11, 2021}} Kalaitzakis made his debut in the [[National Basketball Association|NBA]] on October 19, coming-off from bench with two rebounds in a 127–104 win over the [[2021–22 Brooklyn Nets season|Brooklyn Nets]].{{cite web|title=Bucks begin title defense with 127-104 victory over Nets|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap/_/gameId/401358773|date=October 19, 2021|website=ESPN.com|accessdate=October 19, 2021}} On December 3, he was waived by the Bucks after nine appearances.{{cite web|title=Milwaukee Bucks Sign Wesley Matthews|url=https://www.nba.com/bucks/news/milwaukee-bucks-sign-wesley-matthews|website=NBA.com|date=December 3, 2021|access-date=December 3, 2021}} ===Oklahoma City Thunder / Blue (2021–2022)=== On December 30, 2021, Kalaitzakis was claimed off waivers by the [[Oklahoma City Blue]] of the [[NBA G League]]{{cite web|title=2021-22 NBA G League transactions|url=https://gleague.nba.com/transactions/|website=NBA.com|access-date=December 30, 2021}} where he played in 31 regular season games and averaged 10.1 points, 3.9 rebounds and 2.1 assists in 19.6 minutes per game.{{cite web|title=Thunder Signs Georgios Kalaitzakis and Zavier Simpson to 10-Day Contracts|url=https://www.nba.com/thunder/news/release-10day-220405|website=NBA.com|date=April 5, 2022|access-date=April 5, 2022}} On April 5, 2022, he signed with the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]] for the rest of the season. Kalaitzakis played four games (all starts) for the Thunder, averaging 41.5 minutes and 17.5 points per game.{{Cite magazine|url=https://www.si.com/nba/thunder/news/thunder-end-of-the-year-report-card-georgios-kalaitzakis|title=Thunder End of the Year Report Card: Georgios Kalaitzakis|first=Chris|last=Becker|magazine=Sports Illustrated |date=May 3, 2022}} ===Second stint with Panathinaikos (2022–2023)=== On July 25, 2022, Kalaitzakis signed a two-year contract with [[Panathinaikos B.C.|Panathinaikos]], returning to Greece and reuniting with his twin brother [[Panagiotis Kalaitzakis|Panos]].{{Cite web|title=Panathinaikos officially signs Giorgos Kalaitzakis|url=https://www.eurohoops.net/en/euroleague/1372161/panathinaikos-officially-signs-giorgos-kalaitzakis/|website=Eurohoops|date=July 25, 2022|accessdate=July 5, 2024}} In 26 EuroLeague games (16 starts), he averaged 2 points and 1.1 rebounds in 10 minutes per contest. Additionally, in 29 domestic league matches, he averaged 6.4 points, 1.8 rebounds and 1.2 assists in 13 minutes per contest. On September 4, 2023, Kalaitzakis was released from the Greek powerhouse. ===Tigers Tübingen (2023–2024)=== On December 7, 2023, Kalaitzakis signed a one-year contract with [[Tigers Tübingen]] of the German [[Basketball Bundesliga]].{{Cite web|title=Ein interessanter Name! Georgios Kalaitzakis kommt von Panathinaikos Athen nach Tübingen|url=https://tigers-tuebingen.de/ein-interessanter-name-georgios-kalaitzakis-kommt-von-panathinaikos-athen-nach-tuebingen/|website=Tigers Tübingen|language=de|date=December 7, 2023|accessdate=July 5, 2024}} ===Lietkabelis Panevėžys (2024–2025)=== On July 5, 2024, Kalaitzakis signed a one-year deal with [[BC Lietkabelis|Lietkabelis Panevėžys]] of the [[Lietuvos krepšinio lyga|Lithuanian Basketball League]] (LKL) and the [[EuroCup Basketball|EuroCup]].{{Cite web|title=Panevėžyje – NBA ir Eurolygos patirties turintis graikas|url=https://www.kklietkabelis.lt/panevezyje-nba-ir-eurolygos-patirties-turintis-graikas/|website=BC Lietkabelis|language=lt|date=July 5, 2024|accessdate=July 5, 2024}} ===Maroussi (2025–2026)=== On July 28, 2025, Kalaitzakis returned to Greece, signing a two-year deal with [[Maroussi B.C.|Maroussi]]. === Promitheas Patras (2026–present) === On 24 August 2026, Kalaitzakis signed with [[Promitheas Patras B.C.|Promitheas Patras]] of the [[Greek Basketball League]] (GBL) and the [[Basketball Champions League]] (BCL).{{Cite web |last=Patras |first=Promitheas |date=2026-08-23 |title="Πατρινός" ο Γιώργος Καλαϊτζάκης |url=https://promitheasbc.gr/patrinos-o-giorgos-kalaitzakis/ |access-date=2026-08-24 |website=Προμηθέας Πάτρας Βίκος Cola |language=en-US}} ==National team career== Kalaitzakis was a member of the junior national teams of Greece. With Greece's junior national teams, he played at the [[2015 FIBA Europe Under-16 Championship]], the [[2016 FIBA Europe Under-18 Championship]], and the [[2017 FIBA Europe Under-18 Championship]]. He also played at the [[2018 FIBA Europe Under-20 Championship]], and the [[2019 FIBA Europe Under-20 Championship]], which he led in scoring, with an average of 19.7 points per game.{{Cite web|url=https://www.fiba.basketball/europe/u20/2019/playerstats|title=Players statistics of the FIBA U20 European Championship 2019|website=FIBA.basketball}} ==Career statistics== {{NBA player
